title.en: A fee and a price, and bundles (predicted 4)
title.zh: 入场费加单价，以及捆绑（预测题 4）

description.en: Why a seller with power charges a fee plus a price per use, what to do when its customers differ, and why selling two products only as a bundle can earn more than selling them apart.
description.zh: 有市场势力的卖家为什么要收入场费再按次收费，顾客不一样时怎么办，以及为什么两种产品只捆绑出售能比分开卖赚得更多。

description.en: Keeping the monopoly price per use and adding a fee on top
description.zh: 保持垄断单价，再在上面加一笔入场费

title.en: Predicted question 4, as it could be printed

paras.en: A town has one golf club. Each golfer's demand for rounds per year is $Q = 20 - p$, where $p$ is the price of a round. Each round costs the club \$4 ($MC = 4$).
paras.zh: 某镇只有一家高尔夫俱乐部。每位球手每年打球的需求为 $Q = 20 - p$，其中 $p$ 是每场的价格。每场给俱乐部带来 4 的成本（$MC = 4$）。

paras.en: **a.** If the club charges only a price per round, find the price, the rounds per golfer and the profit per golfer. (3 marks)
paras.zh: **a.** 如果俱乐部只按场收费，求价格、每位球手的场数和每位球手带来的利润。（3 分）

paras.en: **b.** The club instead uses a two-part tariff: an annual membership fee plus a price per round. Find the profit-maximising fee and price per round, and the profit per golfer. Explain why this earns more than (a). (5 marks)
paras.zh: **b.** 俱乐部改用两部收费：年费加每场价格。求使利润最大的年费和每场价格，以及每位球手带来的利润。解释为什么这比 (a) 赚得多。（5 分）

paras.en: **c.** Now half of the golfers are keen ($Q = 20 - p$) and half are casual ($Q = 16 - p$). The club cannot tell them apart and offers one fee and one price per round to all. Compare a price per round of \$4 with \$6, each with the highest fee at which casual golfers still join. Which earns more per pair of golfers (one of each)? (5 marks)
paras.zh: **c.** 现在一半球手是热衷型（$Q = 20 - p$），一半是休闲型（$Q = 16 - p$）。俱乐部分不清谁是谁，对所有人提供同一个年费和同一个每场价格。比较每场 4 和每场 6 两种方案，各配以休闲型球手仍愿入会的最高年费。哪个方案每一对球手（各一位）带来的利润更多？（5 分）

paras.en: **d.** A software firm sells a word processor and a spreadsheet, each costing nothing to supply. Customer A values them at \$120 and \$40, customer B at \$90 and \$70. Find the firm's profit if it prices each product separately, and if it sells only a bundle of both. Explain why bundling raises profit here. (5 marks)
paras.zh: **d.** 某软件公司卖一款文字处理软件和一款电子表格，供给成本都是零。顾客 A 对两者的估值分别是 120 和 40，顾客 B 是 90 和 70。求两种产品分别定价时的利润，以及只卖两者捆绑包时的利润。解释为什么这里捆绑能提高利润。（5 分）

title.en: Why this is a likely question
title.zh: 为什么这道题很可能考

body.en: Non-uniform pricing is a lecture of its own: price discrimination, two-part pricing and bundling. The mock asked third- and second-degree discrimination (its question 3); these are the other two tools.
body.zh: 非统一定价是单独的一讲：价格歧视、两部收费和捆绑。模考考了三级和二级价格歧视（第 3 题）；这里是另外两种工具。

items.en: **One club in town**: it is a monopolist; it chooses its prices.
items.zh: **镇上只有一家俱乐部**：它是垄断者，自己定价。

items.en: **Demand $Q = 20 - p$ per golfer**: the first round is worth almost \$20 to a golfer, the 10th \$10, the 20th nothing. The height of the curve is what each extra round is worth.
items.zh: **每位球手的需求 $Q = 20 - p$**：第一场对球手值将近 20，第 10 场值 10，第 20 场一文不值。曲线的高度就是每多打一场值多少。

items.en: **A two-part tariff**: a fixed fee to join, then a price for each use (a gym, a phone plan, a theme park with paid rides).
items.zh: **两部收费**（two-part tariff）：先交一笔固定的入场费，每用一次再交一次的钱（健身房、手机套餐、游乐园里按项目收费）。

items.en: **Values in (d)** are the most each customer would pay for each product: their *reservation prices*.
items.zh: **(d) 里的估值**是每位顾客对每种产品最多愿付的钱：他们的*保留价格*。

title.en: One price per round, and what it leaves on the table
title.zh: 只按场收费，以及它漏掉了什么

paras.en: If the club charges only a price per round, find the price, the rounds per golfer and the profit per golfer.
paras.zh: 如果俱乐部只按场收费，求价格、每位球手的场数和每位球手带来的利润。

text.en: This is the monopolist of the mock's question 2: marginal revenue equals marginal cost. With demand $p = 20 - Q$, revenue is $(20 - Q)Q$ and $MR = 20 - 2Q$. Setting $MR = 4$ gives 8 rounds at \$12 each: \$8 of profit on each of 8 rounds, 64 per golfer.
text.zh: 这就是模考第 2 题的垄断者：边际收益等于边际成本。需求 $p = 20 - Q$，收益 $(20 - Q)Q$，$MR = 20 - 2Q$。令 $MR = 4$，得 8 场、每场 12：8 场每场赚 8，每位球手 64。

text.en: Look at what this leaves behind. The golfer still keeps the triangle above \$12 (rounds 1 to 8 were worth more than 12 to her): consumer surplus of 32. And rounds 9 to 16 are worth more than their cost of 4 but are not played, because the club will not lower the price for them without lowering it for every round: a deadweight loss. A single price cannot take the surplus without killing some of it.
text.zh: 看看这样漏掉了什么。球手还保留着 12 以上的三角形（第 1 到第 8 场对她都值 12 以上）：消费者剩余 32。第 9 到第 16 场的价值高于成本 4，却没人打，因为俱乐部要为它们降价，就得给每一场都降价：这是无谓损失。单一价格拿剩余时，必然会毁掉一部分剩余。

title.en: The two-part tariff: make the pie as big as possible, then take it
title.zh: 两部收费：先把蛋糕做到最大，再整个拿走

paras.en: The club instead uses a two-part tariff: an annual membership fee plus a price per round. Find the profit-maximising fee and price per round, and the profit per golfer. Explain why this earns more than (a).
paras.zh: 俱乐部改用两部收费：年费加每场价格。求使利润最大的年费和每场价格，以及每位球手带来的利润。解释为什么这比 (a) 赚得多。

text.en: With two prices the club can do two jobs separately. The **price per round** decides how many rounds are played, and so how big the total gain from golf is. The **fee** decides how much of that gain the club takes. The golfer joins as long as the fee is no more than the surplus she gets from playing at the per-round price.
text.zh: 有了两个价格，俱乐部可以把两件事分开做。**每场价格**决定打多少场，也就决定了打球带来的总好处有多大。**年费**决定这份好处俱乐部拿走多少。只要年费不超过她在这个每场价格下打球得到的剩余，球手就会入会。

text.en: So: first make the gain as big as possible. That happens when every round worth more than its cost is played, that is, at a price per round equal to marginal cost, \$4: 16 rounds. Then take all of it with the fee: the whole triangle under demand and above 4, $\frac12 \times 16 \times 16 = 128$. The club earns 128, twice the 64 of part (a), and there is no deadweight loss. It has the same effect as perfect (first-degree) price discrimination.
text.zh: 所以：先把好处做到最大。价值高于成本的每一场都打的时候好处最大，也就是每场价格等于边际成本 4：打 16 场。再用年费把它整个拿走：需求下方、4 以上的整个三角形，$\frac12 \times 16 \times 16 = 128$。俱乐部赚 128，是 (a) 的 64 的两倍，而且没有无谓损失。效果和完全（一级）价格歧视一样。

alt.en: One golfer’s demand Q = 20 − p and marginal cost 4. A single price of 12 (8 rounds) earns the gold rectangle, 64. With the price per round at 4 the golfer plays 16 rounds and her surplus, the green triangle of 128, is taken as the fee.
alt.zh: 一位球手的需求 Q = 20 − p 和边际成本 4。单一价格 12（8 场）只赚到金色矩形 64。每场价格定在 4 时她打 16 场，她的剩余（绿色三角形 128）作为年费被收走。

caption.en: Gold: the single-price profit. Green: everything above marginal cost, which the fee collects.
caption.zh: 金色：单一价格的利润。绿色：边际成本以上的全部，由年费收走。

prompt.en: Why not keep the price per round at \$12 and add a fee on top?
prompt.zh: 为什么不把每场价格保持在 12，再加一笔年费？

feedback.en: The fee can only take the surplus left at the price per round chosen, and a higher price leaves less.
feedback.zh: 年费只能拿走所选每场价格下剩下的剩余，价格越高剩下越少。

label.en: At 12 the golfer's surplus is only 32, so the fee can be at most 32: 64 + 32 = 96 < 128
It is the same either way

feedback.en: The rounds 9 to 16 are lost at 12; at 4 their gain is collected too.
feedback.zh: 每场 12 时第 9 到第 16 场的好处丢了；每场 4 时它们的好处也被收走。

explain.en: A higher price per round shrinks the pie the fee can take. With identical customers, the best price per round is marginal cost.
explain.zh: 每场价格越高，年费能拿的蛋糕越小。顾客都一样时，最好的每场价格就是边际成本。

say.en: (a) A single price: marginal revenue equals marginal cost.
say.zh: (a) 单一价格：边际收益等于边际成本。

say.en: Profit per golfer: the margin times the rounds.
say.zh: 每位球手的利润：每场的利润乘场数。

say.en: (b) The price per round at marginal cost: every round worth more than 4 is played.
say.zh: (b) 每场价格等于边际成本：价值超过 4 的每一场都打。

say.en: The fee: the golfer's whole surplus at that price, the most she would pay to join.
say.zh: 年费：这个价格下球手的全部剩余，也就是她入会最多愿付的钱。

say.en: Profit: the fee, plus nothing on the rounds (each sells at cost).
say.zh: 利润：年费，按场部分不赚（每场按成本卖）。

outro.en: **Answer:** (a) \$12 a round, 8 rounds, \$64 per golfer. (b) A fee of \$128 and \$4 a round: 16 rounds and \$128 per golfer. Pricing rounds at cost makes the total gain as large as possible, and the fee takes all of it, so there is no deadweight loss.
outro.zh: **答案：** (a) 每场 12，8 场，每位球手 64。(b) 年费 128，每场 4：16 场，每位球手 128。按成本给每场定价让总好处最大，年费把它全部拿走，所以没有无谓损失。

prompt.en: The area of the triangle under $p = 20 - Q$ and above 4.
prompt.zh: $p = 20 - Q$ 下方、4 以上的三角形面积。

title.en: When golfers differ: the fee is set by the casual ones
title.zh: 球手不一样时：年费由休闲型决定

paras.en: Half the golfers are keen ($Q = 20 - p$), half casual ($Q = 16 - p$). One fee and one price per round for all. Compare \$4 with \$6 a round, each with the highest fee at which casual golfers still join. Which earns more per pair?
paras.zh: 一半球手是热衷型（$Q = 20 - p$），一半是休闲型（$Q = 16 - p$）。所有人同一个年费、同一个每场价格。比较每场 4 和每场 6，各配以休闲型仍愿入会的最高年费。哪个每对赚得更多？

text.en: With one fee for all, the club has a dilemma. A fee of 128 would take everything from the keen golfers but drive the casual ones away. To keep both, the fee can be no more than the casual golfer's surplus. The keen golfer then pays the same fee and keeps a big surplus.
text.zh: 所有人同一个年费，俱乐部就两难了。年费定 128 能把热衷型的剩余全拿走，但休闲型就不来了。想两类都留住，年费最多只能是休闲型的剩余。热衷型付同样的年费，自己留下一大块剩余。

text.en: Now the price per round becomes a second way to earn from the keen golfers, who play more. Raise it from 4 to 6: the casual golfer's surplus, and so the fee, falls (from 72 to 50), a loss of 22 on each golfer, 44 per pair. But every round now earns \$2, and the pair plays $14 + 10 = 24$ rounds: 48. A net gain of 4. The keen golfer plays more rounds, so a margin per round collects more from her than from the casual one.
text.zh: 这时每场价格就成了从热衷型身上多赚的第二个办法，因为他们打得多。把它从 4 提到 6：休闲型的剩余、也就是年费，就下降（从 72 降到 50），每位少 22，每对少 44。但现在每场赚 2，这一对一共打 $14 + 10 = 24$ 场：48。净多 4。热衷型打得多，所以每场的加价从她身上收得比从休闲型身上多。

alt.en: Two demands, keen Q = 20 − p and casual Q = 16 − p. At 6 a round the casual golfer plays 10 and her surplus, the green triangle of 50, sets the fee; the keen golfer plays 14.
alt.zh: 两条需求：热衷型 Q = 20 − p，休闲型 Q = 16 − p。每场 6 时休闲型打 10 场，她的剩余（绿色三角形 50）决定年费；热衷型打 14 场。

caption.en: The green triangle is the most the casual golfer will pay to join at \$6 a round.
caption.zh: 绿色三角形是每场 6 时休闲型最多愿付的年费。

text.en: Is 6 the best price? Profit per pair at a price $p$ is two fees plus the margin on both golfers' rounds. Its derivative is zero exactly at $p = 6$, so yes. (And serving keen golfers only, with a fee of 128, earns 128 per pair, less than both.)
text.zh: 6 是最好的价格吗？每对的利润 = 两份年费 + 两人所有场次的加价。它的导数正好在 $p = 6$ 处为零，所以是。（只服务热衷型、年费 128，每对赚 128，比两种方案都少。）

say.en: At \$4 a round a casual golfer plays 12 rounds; the fee is her surplus.
say.zh: 每场 4 时休闲型打 12 场；年费就是她的剩余。

say.en: Per pair at \$4: two fees, nothing on the rounds.
say.zh: 每场 4 时每对：两份年费，按场部分不赚。

say.en: At \$6 the casual golfer plays 10 rounds; her surplus, and the fee, is 50.
say.zh: 每场 6 时休闲型打 10 场；她的剩余（也就是年费）是 50。

say.en: Per pair at \$6: two fees plus \$2 on the keen golfer's 14 rounds and the casual one's 10.
say.zh: 每场 6 时每对：两份年费，加上热衷型 14 场、休闲型 10 场每场赚的 2。

outro.en: **Answer:** \$4 a round with a fee of \$72 earns \$144 per pair; \$6 a round with a fee of \$50 earns \$148. Pricing rounds above cost earns more, because the keen golfers, who keep surplus under the common fee, play more rounds.
outro.zh: **答案：** 每场 4、年费 72，每对赚 144；每场 6、年费 50，每对赚 148。把每场价格定在成本以上赚得更多，因为在统一年费下留着剩余的热衷型打得更多。

prompt.en: Two fees of 50, plus \$2 on 24 rounds.
prompt.zh: 两份 50 的年费，再加 24 场每场 2。

title.en: Bundling: selling two products as one
title.zh: 捆绑：把两种产品当一种卖

paras.en: Customer A values the word processor at \$120 and the spreadsheet at \$40, customer B at \$90 and \$70; zero cost. Find the profit with separate prices, and with only a bundle. Explain why bundling raises profit here.
paras.zh: 顾客 A 对文字处理软件估值 120、电子表格 40，顾客 B 是 90 和 70；成本为零。求分别定价时的利润，以及只卖捆绑包时的利润。解释为什么这里捆绑能提高利润。

text.en: Separately, each product has two sensible prices: the lower value (both buy) or the higher (one buys). Word processor: \$90 to both earns 180, \$120 to A earns 120; choose 90. Spreadsheet: \$40 to both earns 80, \$70 to B earns 70; choose 40. Total 260. Each time the firm must price down to the customer who values that product less.
text.zh: 分开卖时，每种产品有两个合理的价格：较低的估值（两人都买）或较高的估值（只有一人买）。文字处理：90 卖给两人得 180，120 只卖给 A 得 120；选 90。电子表格：40 卖给两人得 80，70 只卖给 B 得 70；选 40。合计 260。每一次厂商都得把价格降到估值较低的那位顾客。

text.en: As a bundle: A values both together at $120 + 40 = 160$, B at $90 + 70 = 160$. A bundle price of 160 sells to both: 320. The reason is that the values are **negatively correlated**: A likes the word processor more and the spreadsheet less, B the other way round. In the bundle the differences cancel, so the customers' values for the bundle are closer together than for either product, and the firm can charge close to each customer's full value.
text.zh: 捆绑卖：A 对两者合起来的估值是 $120 + 40 = 160$，B 是 $90 + 70 = 160$。捆绑价 160，两人都买：320。原因是估值**负相关**：A 更喜欢文字处理、不那么在乎表格，B 正好相反。捆在一起，差别相互抵消，两人对捆绑包的估值比对任何单一产品都更接近，厂商于是能收到接近每位顾客的全部估值。

prompt.en: If A valued the two at \$120 and \$70 and B at \$90 and \$40 (positively correlated), would a pure bundle still beat separate prices?
prompt.zh: 如果 A 对两者估值 120 和 70，B 是 90 和 40（正相关），纯捆绑还比分开定价好吗？

feedback.en: Bundling helps by evening out values; with positive correlation there is nothing to even out.
feedback.zh: 捆绑的作用是把估值拉平；正相关时没什么可拉平的。

feedback.en: One bundle price for both: 130 to both earns 260, 190 to A alone earns 190.
feedback.zh: 两人只能是同一个捆绑价：130 卖两人得 260，190 只卖 A 得 190。

label.en: No: bundle values 190 and 130, the best bundle earns 260, the same as separate prices
label.zh: 不会：捆绑估值 190 和 130，最好的捆绑价也只赚 260，和分开定价一样

explain.en: Separate: 90 × 2 + 40 × 2 = 260. Bundle: at most 260. Bundling pays when customers who like one product more like the other less.
explain.zh: 分开：90 × 2 + 40 × 2 = 260。捆绑：最多 260。只有喜欢一种多、另一种就少的顾客，捆绑才划算。

say.en: Word processor alone: \$90 to both beats \$120 to A only.
say.zh: 文字处理单卖：90 卖两人好于 120 只卖 A。

say.en: Spreadsheet alone: \$40 to both beats \$70 to B only.
say.zh: 电子表格单卖：40 卖两人好于 70 只卖 B。

say.en: Profit with separate prices (costs are zero).
say.zh: 分别定价的利润（成本为零）。

say.en: Each customer's value for the bundle.
say.zh: 每位顾客对捆绑包的估值。

say.en: A bundle at \$160 sells to both.

outro.en: **Answer:** separate prices (\$90 and \$40) earn \$260; a bundle at \$160 earns \$320. Values are negatively correlated, so the bundle's values are equal and the firm captures both customers' full value.
outro.zh: **答案：** 分开定价（90 和 40）赚 260；捆绑价 160 赚 320。估值负相关，捆绑包的估值相等，厂商拿到两位顾客的全部估值。

prompt.en: Both customers buy the bundle at 160.
prompt.zh: 两位顾客都以 160 买捆绑包。

paras.en: **b.** Set the price per round at $MC = \$4$ (16 rounds), maximising total surplus; charge a fee equal to the golfer's consumer surplus, $\frac12 \times 16 \times 16 = \$128$. Profit \$128 per golfer, double (a): the club captures all surplus and there is no deadweight loss (as with first-degree price discrimination).
paras.zh: **b.** 每场价格定在 $MC = 4$（16 场），使总剩余最大；年费等于球手的消费者剩余 $\frac12 \times 16 \times 16 = 128$。每位利润 128，是 (a) 的两倍：俱乐部拿走全部剩余，没有无谓损失（与一级价格歧视相同）。

paras.en: **c.** At \$4: fee $=$ the casual golfer's surplus $= \frac12 \times 12^2 = 72$; profit per pair $= 144$. At \$6: fee $= \frac12 \times 10^2 = 50$; rounds $14 + 10 = 24$ earn \$2 each; profit $= 100 + 48 = \$148$. \$6 is better: pricing above cost extracts more from the keen golfers, who keep surplus under a common fee and play more.
paras.zh: **c.** 每场 4：年费 $=$ 休闲型的剩余 $= \frac12 \times 12^2 = 72$；每对利润 144。每场 6：年费 $= \frac12 \times 10^2 = 50$；共 $14 + 10 = 24$ 场，每场赚 2；利润 $= 100 + 48 = 148$。6 更好：高于成本定价能从热衷型身上多收，他们在统一年费下留有剩余、打得更多。

paras.en: **d.** Separately: word processor at \$90 (180), spreadsheet at \$40 (80): \$260. Bundle: both value it at \$160, so a bundle price of \$160 earns \$320. Bundling works because valuations are negatively correlated, which makes the bundle valuations more similar than the separate ones.
paras.zh: **d.** 分开：文字处理 90（180），电子表格 40（80）：260。捆绑：两人估值都是 160，捆绑价 160 赚 320。捆绑有效是因为估值负相关，捆绑后的估值比单个产品的更接近。

text.en: Where the marks are: in (b) why the price per round equals marginal cost; in (c) the profit per pair for both prices; in (d) the words *negatively correlated* with what they mean here.
text.zh: 得分点：(b) 为什么每场价格等于边际成本；(c) 两种价格下每对的利润；(d) 写出*负相关*，并说明它在这里的意思。

title.en: Mixed bundling, and how this connects to price discrimination
title.zh: 混合捆绑，以及它和价格歧视的关系

items.en: **Mixed bundling**: offer the bundle *and* each product alone. It helps when some customers value one product below its cost: they buy just the other, and the firm does not have to give the unwanted product away.
items.zh: **混合捆绑**：既卖捆绑包，*也*单卖每种产品。当有顾客对某种产品的估值低于其成本时有用：他们只买另一种，厂商不必把对方不要的东西白送。

items.en: **All of these are price discrimination in disguise.** A two-part tariff charges heavy users a lower average price per round; a bundle charges each customer close to her own value; the mock's packages (question 3b) let customers sort themselves. Each needs the same two conditions: market power, and no resale.
items.zh: **这些其实都是变相的价格歧视。** 两部收费让多用的人每场平均价格更低；捆绑让每位顾客都付接近自己的估值；模考的套餐（第 3 题 b）让顾客自己选择归类。每一种都需要同样两个条件：有市场势力，且不能转卖。

items.en: **If a question asks for the best price per round with two types** in general, write profit as a function of $p$ as above and set its derivative to zero; then check against serving only the keen type.
items.zh: **如果题目问两类顾客时一般情况下的最优每场价格**，像上面那样把利润写成 $p$ 的函数，令导数为零；再和只服务热衷型的方案比一比。

items.en: Charging the monopoly price per use plus a fee: the fee then takes only the small surplus left.
items.zh: 按垄断价收每次的钱再加年费：这样年费只能拿到剩下的一点剩余。

items.en: With two types, setting the fee at the keen golfer's surplus and forgetting that casual golfers then leave.
items.zh: 两类顾客时把年费定成热衷型的剩余，忘了休闲型会因此离开。

items.en: For bundling, adding the two separate profits instead of comparing them with one common bundle price.
items.zh: 算捆绑时把两种单独的利润相加，而不是和一个统一的捆绑价比较。

prompt.en: A gym's members each have demand $Q = 30 - 2p$ for visits, and a visit costs the gym \$5. With the best two-part tariff, what is the annual fee?
prompt.zh: 健身房每位会员的到访需求为 $Q = 30 - 2p$，每次到访成本 5。最优两部收费下，年费是多少？

explain.en: Price per visit at $MC = 5$: $Q = 20$. Fee = surplus = $\frac12 \times 20 \times (15 - 5) = 100$ (the demand's price intercept is 15).
explain.zh: 每次价格 $= MC = 5$：$Q = 20$。年费 = 剩余 $= \frac12 \times 20 \times (15 - 5) = 100$（需求曲线的价格截距是 15）。

prompt.en: Customer A values a film channel at \$30 and a sports channel at \$10; B values them at \$15 and \$25. Costs are zero. What does the best pure bundle earn from the two customers?
prompt.zh: 顾客 A 对电影频道估值 30、体育频道 10；B 是 15 和 25。成本为零。最好的纯捆绑从两位顾客那里赚多少？

explain.en: Bundle values 40 and 40: price 40 sells to both, 80. Separately: film 30 (or 15 × 2 = 30), sports 25 (or 10 × 2 = 20): 55.
